Reader-facing listing (a promise to support, not completed events or scene instructions):

When the System gives everyone one Slot, Owen Price alone can keep every skill he finds. A supermarket night worker obsessed with indoor climbing, he now needs to get his coworkers out before the roots tearing through the shop trap them inside. Cling lets him cross a wall to a stranded cleaner, but the way back is falling apart. Others must surrender one skill to take another. Owen can add a foothold on empty air to his grip on the wall, combining skills to climb faster through the ranks. If he can get everyone out, there are inhabited terraces above the broken roof, promising help and heights he already wants to climb. His aching arms need to last that long.

World-building material (properties to define, not events to schedule):
The setting: The System arrives everywhere on Earth at once. Its first message appears on phones, tills, televisions and directly in each person’s vision: EVERY PERSON HAS RECEIVED ONE SLOT. CHOOSE WHAT YOU WILL BE ABLE TO DO. Earth remains recognisable, but unfamiliar terrain grows through it along discontinuities: railway cuttings become ravines, lift shafts open into enormous trees, and roads emerge on the sides of forested cliffs. Ordinary life continues wherever people can keep roofs, water and food accessible. Owen’s supermarket becomes a gathering place because much of its stock survives, not because anyone designates it a settlement.

Every person receives exactly one Slot and a choice of starter skills. A skill is a specific magical permission, not a bundle of unrelated abilities. Cling allows controlled adhesion through hands and feet; Anchor holds the user stationary against external force; Kindle ignites suitable material by touch. There are no classes that confer extra skills. Mundane climbing, first aid and mechanical knowledge remain useful without occupying a Slot.

Later skills occur in tangible sources, including patterned seeds from the cliff orchards. Touching an intact source reveals its skill before the person commits. Taking it consumes the source. An ordinary person must release their existing skill to install another; the abandoned skill becomes unavailable, although their memories and mundane expertise remain. Reacquiring it requires another source. Owen can take every skill he finds without releasing any. Unlimited capacity does not supply unlimited seeds, attention, stamina or safe practice.

Each sheet displays Slot Rank. Installing a skill gives no advancement by itself. The System recognises demonstrated control: first successful use under a real environmental demand, materially harder applications, and genuinely new combinations. Repeating an easy manoeuvre stops earning progress, while sustained practice can prepare someone for a harder feat. Higher ranks increase the strength and endurance of installed skills without adding new magical functions. Owen has access to fresh demonstrations and combinations that nobody else can accumulate simultaneously. His advantage is structural, rather than a hidden multiplier.

The newly exposed biome consists of cliff orchards threaded by enormous roots, warm rain channels and hanging gardens. Observable traces include pruned branches, ceramic graft sleeves, sheltered sleeping hollows and handrails placed for bodies smaller than humans. Some paths have been cut deliberately. These are evidence of habitation and interrupted maintenance, not abandoned dungeon decoration.

The underlying explanation is that the orchards are cultivated territory belonging to the Vey, small, furred, many-limbed people whose communities transport pollen, maintain seasonal bridges and argue over access to graft stock. They too have single-skill Slots. Their old quarrel concerns whether distant orchards should remain connected after a root-borne blight crossed a shared bridge. Family marks on sealed paths and newer repair knots preserve that history. Earth’s arrival has broken irrigation routes and separated households. Some Vey initially mistake human buildings for a deliberate invasion; some humans mistake orchard skill-seeds for ownerless loot. Neither belief is reliable.

The Vey know how to cultivate skill-bearing plants, but they do not know who made the System. Whether Earth has moved, the orchard world has expanded, or both have been joined to something larger remains unknown. Nothing currently explains Owen’s exception.
The person's background: Owen Price is a supermarket night worker in his twenties who takes indoor bouldering far too seriously. Before the arrival, his concerns are finishing his shift, avoiding Leanne’s disapproval and reaching the climbing wall before it becomes crowded. Climbing has taught him balance, foot placement and how to work through a difficult movement, not exceptional strength or fearlessness.
The magical possibility to support: Everyone receives exactly one Slot, but Owen alone has unlimited capacity within his Slot. He can install every skill he obtains without releasing any existing skill. Other people must relinquish their installed skill to replace it; their memories and mundane expertise remain, but reacquiring the abandoned magic requires another source. Owen still needs sources, practice, stamina and attention. His retained skills create ever more opportunities for genuinely new demonstrations and combinations, letting him advance faster than nearby single-skill users without a hidden multiplier.
The system, The Slot System: The arrival message appears worldwide on active screens and directly in human vision: EVERY PERSON HAS RECEIVED ONE SLOT. CHOOSE WHAT YOU WILL BE ABLE TO DO. Personal sheets silently report Slot count, capacity, installed skills and Slot Rank, independently of anyone’s approval. Touching an intact skill source identifies its permission before commitment; taking the skill consumes the source. Installation earns no advancement. Demonstrated control under real environmental demand, materially harder applications and genuinely new combinations earn progress. Easy repetition eventually stops contributing, although practice prepares harder feats. Higher ranks strengthen and extend installed abilities without adding unrelated magical functions. There are no classes granting extra skills.
Its appearance: Still white lettering appears against a faint charcoal field in Owen’s vision, echoed by the interrupted displays during arrival. His first sheet reads: OWEN PRICE; SLOT COUNT: 1; SLOT CAPACITY: UNLIMITED; INSTALLED SKILLS: NONE; SLOT RANK: 1. Later changes update the relevant lines without a speaking guide or celebratory spectacle.
Its advancement span: 8 steps. Strongest known: The highest locally attested practitioner is a Vey seasonal-bridge keeper at counted Rank 8. Their sole skill, Threadline, can sustain temporary cords across a broad ravine through prolonged bridge work. This is the strongest rank Owen learns about, not proof of a final ceiling or worldwide maximum.
The protagonist starts at rank 1 of 8
What advancement enables: Cling gains the strength and endurance to hold through harder loads and violent weather. Air Step provides a stronger brief foothold, supporting more demanding crossings while still requiring recovery of breath before reuse. Threadline gains tensile strength and duration, making dependable temporary routes possible with learned control. Additional functions require additional skills: Owen’s eventual interest in Load Share concerns spreading weight across his lines, not a function that rank alone grants.
The world's danger: Earth remains recognisable but is intersected by cultivated cliff terrain whose broken roots, rain channels and routes threaten access to shelter, food and water. The Vey’s damaged irrigation and separated households intersect with human survival needs. An older dispute over root-borne blight, frightened assumptions about invasion and human removal of skill-seeds complicate cooperation. Owen can reach places his companions cannot, but personal mobility alone cannot produce a safe communal route.

Pending story intentions (constraints, not facts to declare):
Initialize before the opening's actions, retaining capabilities already owned there; its acquisitions, completed tests, meetings and discoveries have not happened. Support the later possibilities without declaring their occurrence or adding access restrictions.
Opening:
Chapter 1 contains scenes 1–4, approximately 900 words each, for approximately 3,600 words total. It uses close third person through Owen and covers one connected escape, leaving room for him to react afterward.

Scene 1: Owen is finishing a night shift when his supervisor, Leanne, catches him revising a climbing route on his phone instead of facing shelves. His hobby has made him attentive to balance and movement, not unusually strong or fearless. He wants to finish work and reach the climbing wall before it gets crowded. The System message interrupts every active display. Messages from people elsewhere briefly establish that the event is worldwide. Then a root tears through the shop floor, tilting the loading corridor and cutting off the staff exit. Owen’s first personal sheet reads: OWEN PRICE; SLOT COUNT: 1; SLOT CAPACITY: UNLIMITED; INSTALLED SKILLS: NONE; SLOT RANK: 1. Leanne’s sheet says SLOT CAPACITY: 1. Their comparison establishes the exception without explaining it. A cleaner, Dev, is stranded beyond the widening break.

Scene 2: Owen considers Anchor, which could keep him safe on the shifting floor, and Kindle, which seems useful if the power stays out. He chooses Cling because he can see a route along the wall to Dev, and because the possibility of actually climbing that wall catches him despite the danger. He makes the selection with shaking hands. Cling does not move him automatically: an overloaded wrist hurts, and a bad body position still peels him away. Leanne chooses Anchor to hold a rolling stock cage while the remaining staff squeeze past. Owen uses familiar foot placement and unfamiliar adhesion to cross the damaged corridor and reach Dev. Successful control raises his Slot Rank to 2; he feels the change when his hands stop trembling under the same load. From Dev’s side, however, he discovers that the root has pulled the return wall apart. He can get back alone by a difficult detour, but Dev cannot follow him.

Scene 3: The exposed root carries a graft sleeve and a translucent seed. A touch identifies AIR STEP: a brief foothold on empty air, usable again after the user recovers their breath. The placement suggests cultivation, but Owen has nobody to ask. He takes it because the broken return route now has a possible solution. His sheet changes to INSTALLED SKILLS: CLING, AIR STEP; SLOT COUNT remains 1. Both abilities still work. His first attempt wastes the foothold before he transfers his weight. He rehearses the timing low over a stable ledge, where failure is recoverable, then commits to the gap. Cling lets him hold the launch position; Air Step lets him change direction across empty space; Cling catches the far wall. The successful combination advances him to Slot Rank 3. This is more than a private discovery: he has carried a line across the gap, and Leanne can anchor its safe end.

Scene 4: The escape takes effort after the magical breakthrough. Owen secures the line around a surviving structural upright rather than asking anyone to trust his grip indefinitely. Leanne remains fixed while Dev crosses with help from the others. Owen returns along the line instead of showing off another leap. Once everyone reaches the shop’s intact frontage, the consequences arrive: his forearms ache, Dev needs treatment, and Leanne wants to know whether taking the seed destroyed someone’s crop. Their sheets show that she remains at Rank 2 while Owen has reached Rank 3. He tells the group that he can hold more than one skill and offers to scout, but refuses an immediate climb while exhausted. Through the torn roof he can see terraces, moving lanterns and rainwater running down a built channel. The chapter ends with his changed desire: once he has rested, he wants to reach that inhabited place, both to find help and to learn what else he could become.
Later possibilities:
Chapter 2, scenes 5–8, approximately 3,600 words: The intact shop becomes a temporary refuge through ordinary work—treating injuries, checking food and finding usable water. Owen and Leanne investigate the orchard channel because the taps have stopped. Owen’s combined movement skills let him inspect an elevated blockage, but reaching it does not tell him how to repair it. He finds a diverted irrigation gate, fresh tool marks and a frightened Vey searching for a missing relative. The chapter changes his objective from collecting useful things to making contact with someone whose home has also been damaged. Leanne’s repeated, increasingly demanding use of Anchor establishes that single-skill people can become formidable specialists.

Chapter 3, scenes 9–12, approximately 3,600 words: Contact develops through shared work and uncertain gestures rather than instant translation. The Vey, Serri, needs access to a stranded nursery before its grafts dry out. Owen needs permission to draw water without ruining someone else’s supply. Each can reach places the other cannot safely manage. Repairing the channel earns a limited water-sharing agreement, and Serri offers a cultivated Threadline seed in return for help reaching the nursery. Threadline produces a temporary tensile cord between touched surfaces. Owen wants it because carrying rope nearly defeated the first rescue. He installs it, but initially makes lines that slacken when his concentration shifts. Taking the skill is immediate; making it dependable is a chapter-level problem.

Chapter 4, scenes 13–16, approximately 3,600 words: The nursery expedition requires Owen to combine adhesion, air footholds and temporary lines while Serri identifies safe grafts and dangerous roots. The resulting advancement carries him ahead of his companions, but a route that suits him proves unsuitable for people carrying water and children. A failed line drops supplies onto a lower terrace and costs the group a long retrieval. Nobody loses earned ranks or acquired skills. Owen instead loses daylight and confidence, and must help build a slower, partly mundane route. His private pursuit of beautiful movement begins to become a desire to make extraordinary places accessible to other people.

Chapter 5, scenes 17–20, approximately 3,600 words: The repaired route reaches a sealed orchard boundary. Serri’s relatives want it reopened to reunite households; another Vey community fears renewed blight. Human scavengers have also begun removing skill-seeds without understanding the grafts. Owen’s mobility makes him useful to every side without making him the rightful decision-maker. He investigates the cut bridges with a local cultivator and discovers an active diseased root beyond the seal. Access to further skills now depends on whether he spends his time helping protect the orchard or simply takes what he can carry. He chooses the slower cooperative route because its people and continued cultivation matter to the future he wants.

Chapter 6, scenes 21–24, approximately 3,600 words: A storm drives runoff through the damaged boundary toward both the nursery and the shop. Owen uses his broader skill set to move between isolated work parties, while Leanne’s stronger Anchor and Vey specialist skills handle loads he cannot. The resolution is a working diversion and a traversable evacuation route, not victory over the whole apocalypse. Owen’s counted advancement continues to outpace the people around him because each new skill opens further meaningful combinations. His next desired capability is Load Share, a grafted skill that could spread weight across his temporary lines; he has seen its source in the nursery and understands why its cultivators will not surrender it casually.

Beyond this opening arc, greater rank could let Owen cling through violent weather, sustain longer crossings and build temporary routes through moving terrain. New skills would expand what he can attempt, but he must still choose where to go, whom to help and what to practise. Injury, failed expeditions and lost equipment can delay him without confiscating his defining advantage. His accumulated skills, knowledge of routes and relationships survive those setbacks. The larger promise is not merely that he can own every power: it is that he can eventually explore—and bring others into—places no single-skill person could cross alone.

System apocalypse. When the System arrives, every person on Earth receives exactly one Slot for one skill. The protagonist, a man in his twenties, receives a Slot that can hold as many skills as he can take. Invent the rest.

By default the world is a place people live in, not an administration. Supplied motives and mechanics take precedence over defaults; leave unspecified advancement quotas and additional cast open. Declare observable forms, activity and historical traces through manifests_as, separately from undisclosed explanations in claim.content.

Start with `litharness world vocabulary`, which tells you every predicate and role the world's language admits, and `litharness world summary`, which tells you what is already there. Declare related facts together with `litharness world declare-batch --records '<JSON array>'`, about twenty-five records per batch, using the vocabulary's record fields and passing the JSON as one literal argument.
Inspect relevant entities with `litharness world query --subjects <id> <id>`, optionally `--predicate <name>`; it returns at most fifty records per page, with next_offset for `--offset` and a selection hash to detect changes between pages. Run `litharness world check` as you go and fix what it names.
Everything you declare is a proposal. Accepting it into the book is somebody else's act, so declare what the book needs and keep it coherent. World rules describe how the world works, and manifestations describe in-world forms. Use wants for current desires, voice_tag for speaking manner and disposition for ordinary temperament or habits; these are changeable character assertions. Beliefs use believes edges to claims. A character's actual magical constraints, physiology or curses remain world rules; separate these from personality even when supplied in the same passage. Future scene actions, explanations and endings belong in story plans, not world rules.

Something in this world grants what people can do, and a ladder belongs to whatever hands out its rungs: name that thing, declare it as this world's system, and give it the ladder; the line the book prints has that ladder's word and the system's grants for its columns and nothing else, because a sheet that prints other numbers is a position in no system and leaves the one you declared unfinished. The line the book prints when a standing changes may carry a second phrase, in the system's words, for a grant gained.
Declare what the system grants, in what order and what each takes, each grant countable and named in short plain words with no digits in them; at least one of them needs another one first, or what you have declared is a list rather than a graph; the engine accepts five to eight grants per system.
Let entry-level capabilities be useful without separately acquired perception or control grants; fundamental handling can be part of the capability. Use numerical prerequisite depths only when the source supplies them; ownership uses one and rank requirements refer to rank rungs.
Use a system-following status sheet with show_unheld set to false unless the author's brief explicitly requests a complete skill tree on the page. Declaring a grant does not give it to the viewpoint character or require its introduction in chapter one.
Declare a permanent fork only when the supplied story specifies mutually exclusive paths, with its ways, grants and opening rungs; putting one resource into some upgrades does not permanently exclude the others. A way may have manifests_as and requires edges for grants at a depth.
Where the system hands out points that people put into its grants, declare the points as a grant of its own that says per_rung how many every rung gives, and say on each grant how many it takes; a grant the rungs hand out is never gained or deepened, and a grant is not offered until those points are there.
On a capability, use growth_limit when supplied mechanics establish its growth: 1 for ownership only, the explicit positive maximum when given, or open when repeatable gains or investments have no supplied cap. A requirement alone does not establish repeatability. Leave unspecified growth undeclared.
Where the concept says the protagonist starts at a rank, declare them stands_at that rank, counted from the lowest; where it says they start unranked, declare no stands_at for them.

Establish which people the viewpoint character can understand and be understood by, including any translation mechanism or language barrier the supplied story relies on. Briefly report what you built and left open.

Every sentence can be followed the first time it is read.
Establish where the viewpoint character is and who the relevant people are to them; make spatial relationships clear before an action depends on them.
Give unfamiliar names and terms enough context to grasp their meaning in the scene, including a brief explanation when needed.
Let the reader follow what the viewpoint character notices, knows and believes, including uncertainty, before a choice depends on it.
Keep the order of events and the connections between them clear.
Use clear references so the reader knows who perceives or acts and what changes.

Emotions and assumptions shape what the viewpoint character notices, expects and chooses. Make room for the relationships, places and concerns that give those choices meaning; a passage can establish these without advancing an external event.
The opening shows what this book is offering: something a person could come to be able to do, and somewhere the reader has not been. A reader who reaches the end of the opening scene without seeing either has been given no reason to start another.
The reader is measuring themselves against the offer, and that is the whole of why they are here. A power with one use invites nobody in, and neither does one the reader meets as a summary of what it could be rather than on the page. A story that names its own ceiling has told the reader where to stop.
Use relative scale and duration for ordinary description. Give an exact quantity only when a character must compare, spend or act against that value, or a required system display gives it; do not manufacture a calculation or countdown to justify incidental detail, treat a number in a plan as an instruction to narrate it, or change established values and their arithmetic when leaving a quantity unspoken.

A power that is spent, used up or traded away costs the reader the thing they came for: what this genre's reader collects is what the person KEEPS.

The bridge executes only the commands this task permits, without a shell. This task exposes no MCP resources. Do not call list_mcp_resources, list_mcp_resource_templates or read_mcp_resource.
